name: Michael "5000" Watts
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 crunk — Michael "5000" Watts (the `houston-screw` lane's research section)
notes: ⛔ **A producer entry, and the workflow it models is the commercial one** — the north-side Swishahouse board that turned the treatment into a product and put it on major-label releases. Where DJ Screw's entry is the treatment itself, this one is the treatment *plus the source record it was applied to*, which is why `session.bpm` spans 58–80: the research states both bands, "output tempo 58–70 quarter-note BPM after treatment; source records 66–80 half-time", and this entry is the only one in the batch that has to hold both. The genre's inherited `modes` are where the two stages resolve. ▶ **The transpose is authored as register, at the classic depth.** "Source key transposed down 2–4 semitones" moves every note down, so melody, chords, bass and 808 all sit two to three semitones under the genre's floors — deeper than OG Ron C's pitch-light variant, shallower than nothing else in the lane. A key name is a label rather than a pitch, so `session.keys` is untouched. ▶ **"Chop events" is three parameters, and they are set below Screw's and well below Ron C's.** `kick.beatSkipProb` 0.20, `snare.clusterProb` 0.26 at 2–3 hits, and stop-time as `dropOutBeats` at 0.85 for 4 beats — the highest stop-time probability in the batch, because the research places his holds specifically "at section boundaries", which is exactly what that transition is. ⛔ **`bass808.monoCutSelf` is `false`: "warmer, longer sub; the low end is boosted as part of the aesthetic."** A sub that the next note does not cut is what "longer" means in MIDI terms. `lowPassed` carries the warmth and sits on the engine's deferral register. The bass rhythm stays `mirror_kick` at 0.96 because a held-note rhythm emits one note per chord and saturates. ▶ **"A second render of the same MIDI" is authored as sameness.** `melody.loopVerbatim` is on, `endVariation` is off, and `arrangement.transitions.switchUpProb` falls to 0.06 — the lowest here. A screwed alternate is not a different arrangement; it is the same arrangement again, slower and lower, which is precisely what the research asks a generator mode to be. ▶ **The doubled vocal phrase is "the main added figure", so the counter is the busiest thing this model authors** — `densityRatio` up to 0.68, `octave_echo` at weight 6, a quarter-note echo. It is the one layer that is genuinely *added* rather than transformed. ⚠ **`confidence` is medium, following the research's high-medium.** Sourced: both tempo bands, his role in spreading and naming the style, the transpose depth, the chop/skip/stop-time vocabulary, the low-end boost, the unaltered-and-re-ordered source material, the doubled vocal phrase, and the album-length alternate as a deliverable. INFERRED: every probability and velocity figure, and `melody.timbreHint` — the research names no instrument for him at all, and `detuned_bell` is this model's reading of "transposed down 2–4 semitones" applied to a bell layer, not something the source says. ⚠ **Fill fingerprint.** `gapProb` 0.28 / `descendProb` 0.65 / `rampJitter` 13 over 8th-triplets, even grouping — the most consistently descending roll in the band, which is the falling-pitch signature of the treatment applied to a fill. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts.
